column2: The Game of Reavers: the North of the Empire
You and [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] are racing to plunder the ports of the North of the Empire. Whoever carries off 50 worth of loot first wins the game, and the brethren will sing of it.
Loot the ports of the North of the Empire before [FromFrom.GetFirstName] does: a tribe is worth 1, a castle 2, a city or temple 4. You need 50. The game ends after five years.

Hunt Down [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
A navy has sent [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] with a fleet to sweep you from the sea. Sink [FromFrom.GetHerHim] before [FromFrom.GetSheHe] sinks you.
Defeat the admiral's army in battle within two years. Losing a battle to [FromFrom.GetHerHim] fails the mission.
Map the Coast of [FromFrom.GetName]
The members of [Root.Society.GetName] sail out to chart the far coasts of the world, to keep the League's maps true and to find the riches and adventures that lie beyond them.
To complete this mission, lead a fleet yourself into the sea zone of §Y[FromFrom.GetName]§!.
Raid the Tombs of [FromFrom.GetName]
The members of [Root.Society.GetName] are not above a little tomb robbing, for the gold of the dead kings of Nehekhara and for the tales they can tell at the League's tables.
To complete this mission, use the §YExploration§! casus belli to loot the tombs of [FromFrom.GetName].
Found a Colony at [FromFrom.GetName]

[Root.Society.GetName] has granted you a charter to found a colony at [FromFrom.GetName], on the far shores where the jungle meets the sea. It is held by foreigners who will not give it up without a fight.
To complete this mission, win the county of §Y[FromFrom.GetName]§! within ten years.
Admiralty
Captain

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The brethren are bored, and bored brethren cut each other's throats. So we have a game for you: the Game of Reavers. You and [pirate_rival.GetTitledFirstName] will race each other to the richest ports of the coast I name. Whoever carries off fifty worth of plunder first is the better reaver, and the brethren will drink to the winner and laugh at the loser for a year.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I accept. Let the best reaver win!

A message has come from [From.GetTitledFirstName], nailed to the mast of a captured ship: [From.GetSheHe] has challenged you to the Game of Reavers. The two of you will race to plunder the same coast, and the first to carry off fifty worth of loot wins. Refusing is not an option, not if you want the brethren to sail with you again.
Then we race.

The last chest is aboard, and the tally is done: you have won the Game of Reavers. In every pirate den from Sartosa to the Sea of Claws the brethren will drink to your name, and [pirate_rival.GetTitledFirstName] will have to listen to it.
Drink up, lads!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has carried off fifty worth of plunder first, and won the Game of Reavers. In every pirate den the brethren are laughing at you.
Let them laugh. Next time.
[pirate_rival.GetTitledFirstName] is dead, and the Game of Reavers died with [pirate_rival.GetHerHim]. The brethren grant you a share of the glory, but it is not the same.
A pity. I was winning.
Five years have passed, and nobody has won the Game of Reavers. The brethren have lost interest and gone back to plain robbery.
A poor showing.

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

You have made yourself a name, and names attract admirals. Our spies say a navy is fitting out a fleet at [admiral_port.GetName] to sweep you from the sea. If you let it sail, it will come for you. If you go out to meet it and sink it, the brethren will know you as a captain worth following.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Let the admiral come. I will be waiting.
The admiral's fleet is broken. Burning hulks drift on the swell, and the survivors are rowing for home with your name on their lips. No navy will send another for a while.
Who rules the waves now?
The admiral has beaten you. Your ships are holed and your crews scattered, and the brethren are already asking whether you are still worth following.
Curses!
Two years have passed, and the admiral's fleet is still afloat. The navy calls it a victory, and the brethren call it cowardice.
Curses!

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

Our charts of the waters off [exploration_target.GetName] are out of date: the coast has shifted, the reefs have moved, or the last mapmaker drew it drunk. Would you take your ships out and chart it for the League? If you seek to impress [Root.Society.GetName], sail there yourself.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
At last you have charted the waters of [Root.Location.GetName], every reef and shoal of them. The mapmakers of [Root.Society.GetName] will be grateful.
Finally!

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The tombs of [my_war_target.GetName] are full of the gold of dead kings, and the dead kings who guard it are slow. A member of the League with a strong arm and a stronger stomach could bring back a fortune, and a tale to tell at our tables.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

It is time you founded a colony of your own. The League holds a charter for [my_war_target.GetName], a port on the far shores held by foreigners who will not give it up without a fight. Take it within ten years, and the charter is yours.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will take [my_war_target.GetName].
I will take Aruk, and Sudenburg will rise again.
The flag of your house flies over [From.GetName]. The colony is founded, and the League has written your name in its rolls of founders.
A new land for my people!
Ten years have passed, and the colony was never founded. The League has given the charter to someone else.
Another time.
Let the others play their game. I have a ship to keep.
I am no admiral. Let the captains squabble over it.
Hoist the sails. I will chart that coast.
Charts are for clerks. Find another fool.
The dead keep their gold badly. I will take it.
I will not wake the kings of Nehekhara.
I have no wish to rule a stockade at the end of the world.
